key_insight: Researchers co-designed a spiking neural network and custom neuromorphic hardware around a dual memory pathway, achieving much better efficiency without sacrificing performance. The result delivers over 4× higher throughput and about 5× better energy efficiency while using 40–60% fewer parameters.
problem_solved: Neuromorphic AI systems often struggle to balance accuracy, speed, energy use, and model size when deployed on specialized hardware. This paper addresses the gap between algorithm design and chip architecture by making both work together from the start.
method: Designed a spiking neural network with two memory pathways to better match hardware constraints and computation patterns.
Co-optimized the model and a custom neuromorphic chip so the network structure fits the device architecture efficiently.
Reduced parameter count while preserving strong performance, improving throughput and energy efficiency on hardware.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that algorithm–hardware co-design can unlock major gains in real-world deployment efficiency. It points to a practical path for building faster, lower-power neuromorphic systems with smaller models.

paper_title: Algorithm–hardware co-design of neuromorphic networks with dual memory pathways
paper_authors: Pengfei Sun, Zhe Su, Jascha Achterberg, Giacomo Indiveri, Dan F. M. Goodman
